approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with an independent policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch supplies its highest-scoring half. The strongest eligible records from a memory of thirty-two accepted elites join them with their original strings and scores. Historical records receive decreasing weights as they accumulate fitting exposures, while current and historical loss shares retain their inherited totals. The policy fits weighted squared error toward frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, with each positive target individually capped at zero. Up to twelve clipped Adam steps retain the final policy. It generates complete SMILES directly from that policy and fills each batch in draw order using chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection.
approach.novelty: Add one attachment-specific admission rule: withhold a newly sampled molecule when a saturated carbon bonded to chlorine, bromine or iodine is also bonded to a neutral oxygen connecting two carbons. Continue drawing from the same policy to fill the batch. This addresses the observed chloromethyl-ether and related bromoether forms without assigning a general preference to fewer halogens, smaller molecules or different ring cores. The earlier scaffold quotas broadened batches but lost final score; this gate has no scaffold quota. Earlier halogen constraints excluded direct heteroatom-halogen bonds while allowing carbon-bound halogens, so they would permit the attachment targeted here. The claim is removal of this precisely defined form with score non-inferiority, not a claim that every admitted molecule is stable or that removing the form improves reward.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-c2ef5c1d5a78 admits chemically valid direct-policy strings without screening the neighborhood of a carbon-halogen bond, so its stream includes the oxygen-adjacent saturated heavy-halide attachment identified in its molecular assessment. Its three actual summary.json/run.log pairs confirm all fifteen sessions completed, macro mean 0.5227052024221274 and population SD 0.02007213966556548; its paired mean change over its own Parent is +0.005049995009632324 with one losing seed. The passive audit recorded in runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0012-11-improve-L03-admission-opportunity-audit.json applies the exact proposed atom predicate to all supplied trajectories: five matching molecules among 4,350 optimizer appearances and zero among 150 initial appearances. Four are chloromethyl ethers in seed 1 drd2_docking at evaluations 249, 263, 290 and 297, with actual scores 0.9999972778697218, 0.9757214553096967, 0.9999945879063337 and 0.9999994163676008; the fifth is an oxygen-adjacent ring C(F)(Br) form in seed 1 sitagliptin_mpo at evaluation 287, score 0.0000024597842258404413. None improved its contemporaneous incumbent. This is a sparse, late opportunity, and high recorded rewards demonstrate score compatibility rather than validated chemical stability. Existing generation receipts total 35,568 raw sequences, 32,647 RDKit-valid draws, 21,191 canonical-novel draws and 16,841 capacity discards; only sixteen of 435 batches needed extra sampling. Parent raw rejected and surplus strings were not retained, so their attachment prevalence cannot be reconstructed. Siblings n-33f9aab34e21 and n-ada44205946f delivered more cores but lost paired endpoint means by 0.01445797260349535 and 0.014326451619946648, respectively. Nodes n-079af8c4a86b and n-dfffb2c8d0b0 confirmed carbon-directed halogen constraints but lost score, and their predicate did not resolve the carbon neighborhood targeted here.
hypothesis: Reject a complete, RDKit-valid, canonically novel policy draw before emission when it contains a neutral divalent C-O-C linkage whose adjacent neutral tetrahedral carbon has a single bond to terminal neutral Cl, Br or I; continue the inherited bounded direct-policy refill with all learning and token sampling unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Two late attachment rejections removed the targeted forms while preserving every score-progress trace.
finding_summary.insights:
The evidence distinguishes direct admission changes from later search changes. Only two molecules were directly rejected; the other three matching parent appearances disappeared after accepted feedback and learning changed. Positive raw draws and the two same-stream replacements show that exclusion was exercised, while exact no-action sessions and pre-rejection prefixes locate the intervention at admission. This narrows the earlier attachment question: a carbon-bound halogen can still require a specific oxygen/carbon neighborhood test, while ordinary aryl halides, carbon-fluorine bonds and oxygen linkages continue to be admitted.

Preserved scores have a limited but clear explanation. Both interventions were late, the removed parent examples had not improved their incumbents, and neither replacement nor any of the 48 identities appearing only in the child's affected sessions produced a new incumbent. The test establishes delivery of the specified chemistry without losing observed progress. It does not establish a reward gain or show that earlier, more frequent exclusions would be equally inexpensive. Iodine and haloalkyl-ester contexts had no observed opportunities.

The molecular assessment still describes ring-rich medicinal scaffolds with unresolved size, linker and reactive-form variation, and 843 generated appearances with unassigned perceived tetrahedral centres. Eliminating this attachment leaves those gaps open. The useful next question is whether precise form control can preserve incumbent progress when opportunities occur more often. Reduced raw motif prevalence, greater stability and practical synthesis remain separate claims requiring their own evidence.
finding_summary.results:
Across 435 completed batches, the raw policy stream contained four molecules with the specified oxygen-adjacent saturated carbon–heavy-halogen attachment. Two arrived after the batch was full and were discarded anyway. The other two—a chloromethyl ether and a cyclic oxygen-adjacent carbon bearing fluorine and bromine—were actively withheld and replaced by nonmatching samples from the same draw stream. No targeted form reached any of the 4,350 optimizer evaluations, compared with five matching appearances in the parent. Both replacements entered the next training update with their original sampled strings and real accepted scores.

All fifteen task sessions finished. Mean final Top-1 remained 0.522705, with population seed deviation 0.020072; the paired change was exactly zero in each seed and task. Mean recorded AUC remained 0.405593, and every recorded best-so-far trace was unchanged. This meets the registered 0.002 endpoint non-inferiority allowance on the complete panel. Thirteen sessions reproduced the parent's entire molecular records; the affected sessions retained identical prefixes through evaluations 248 and 286 before diverging.

Both active batches filled without another sampling call. Overall raw generation stayed at 35,568 draws, including 32,647 valid strings; extra calls remained 23 across sixteen batches. Duplicates rose by seven, so exclusion did not improve raw generation quality. Measured batch-generation time totaled 32.164 seconds versus 24.745 for the parent, including 6.324 seconds in the structural predicate and 0.471 seconds in recorded receipt regions. These measurements describe the runs, rather than isolating a causal overhead.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal scaffolds retain undefined stereochemistry and uneven control of size, linkers and reactive forms.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-f5484e31d41d produces phenyl/pyridyl carboxamides, decorated quinazolines, aromatic molecules bearing cyclic amines, sulfonyl-linked piperazines, and varied amide, amidine and sulfur-containing structures. All five objectives and all three seeds were inspected: 4,350 optimizer appearances and 150 fixed-initial appearances for this node, with the same complete Parent panel. Passive RDKit readings of optimizer appearances give medians of 26 heavy atoms, 368.41 Da, three rings and three aromatic rings; the heavy-atom range is 3 to 90. The digest ring-closure rates are 0.9805 to 0.9966 and aromatic-presence rates 0.9460 to 0.9931; these are string-presence rates, not fractions of atoms or RDKit ring counts. Saturated-ring chemistry is present in 1,294 appearances, so the output is neither ring-deficient nor exclusively aromatic. There are 2,806 distinct nonempty exact Murcko scaffolds, versus 2,813 in Parent n-c2ef5c1d5a78. This supports broad whole-panel exploration, while several successful families concentrate strongly on one core. Exact Murcko differences can also reflect linker or ring-substitution topology and do not establish useful pharmacological diversity. Many leading structures have ordinary, apparently makeable medicinal-chemistry motifs. The questionable synthesis assessment concerns the mixture as a whole: unusual attachment states, activated functional handles, and very large or elaborate outliers remain, without demonstrated routes or stability. The structures do not establish experimental activity, solution microstates or developability. The stereochemical gap is concrete: 843 optimizer appearances contain RDKit-perceived unassigned tetrahedral centres, totaling 1,428 centres, while none has an assigned tetrahedral centre, an @ marker or a directional alkene marker. These are representation observations, not evidence that assigning stereochemistry would improve any score. Compared with the Parent, the specified neutral C-O-C/adjacent saturated-carbon/terminal Cl, Br or I form occurs in zero Child optimizer appearances versus five Parent appearances; initial appearances contain none in either panel. Thirteen complete paired sessions retain identical molecule/score records. The differing records are confined to seed-1 drd2_docking and seed-1 sitagliptin_mpo, and all fifteen recorded final-best values are unchanged. This is a narrow observed output difference, not a general chemical-stability finding or an activation judgment. One sulfonyl fluoride elsewhere in the panel remains a distinct functional handle, illustrating why non-carbon halogen bonding alone is not a makeability verdict. No objective lacks trajectories. Numerical structural readings and every digest-to-trajectory join are recorded in runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0012-11-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json, produced by the adjacent passive audit script after reading all 9,000 Child/Parent records. The report uses existing oracle scores only; it does not rescore molecules or infer unobserved target structures.

per_task.generated_character: Across 870 optimizer appearances the median molecule has 24 heavy atoms, molecular weight 333.37 Da and three rings. The twelve digest leaders are much more consistent than the full set: 23 to 25 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings each, and an amide in every structure. Seed 0 contributes an acetylamino indole bearing a benzyl carboxamide; seed 1 contributes pyridylmethyl benzamides with anilino or pyridone-containing appendages; seed 2 contributes pyridyl ethers bearing an anilide. These are largely conventional connected aromatic amide structures with modest appendages. The whole set also includes tiny charged fragments, large polycyclic structures and repeated amide/aryl expansions. All 900 molecule/score records, including initial observations, match the Parent across the three seeds.
liabilities: Large repeated amide/aryl assemblies add size and conformational burden without the observed reward of the smaller leaders.

The final alpha-bromoacrylamide at seed-2 evaluation 295 contains an activated unsaturated acyl group and scores 0.06933217991151693. Its absence from the screened oxygen-adjacent saturated-halide class does not establish benign reactivity.

The high N-O-linked acyl compound and sulfinamide show that unusual heteroatom attachment can coexist with useful scores. The latter has an unassigned perceived stereocentre; neither should be labeled unmakeable solely from the bond type.
missing_features: Many proposals lack the compact aromatic-ring/amide/short-linker balance shared by the leaders; adding more amides or retaining only a small fragment loses that arrangement.

The leading structures lack saturated ring alternatives to their aromatic frameworks. The data do not establish that such alternatives are rewarded or identify a unique missing target core; the supported gap is reliable preservation of the useful attachment pattern while changing the surrounding framework.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide at evaluation 9 scores 0.3051048083696145; the seed-0 acetylamino-indole benzylamide at evaluation 152 scores 0.43351949803907636. The seed-1 pyridylmethyl benzamide/pyridone at evaluation 273 scores 0.4767312946227961, and the seed-2 ethylpyridyl ether/anilide at evaluation 271 scores 0.5. These examples associate higher reward with a compact aromatic amide arrangement, rather than a unique ring identity. Both extremes fail: the tiny anionic N=C=S fragment scores 5.670115669739515e-23, while the large repeated amide/bicyclic-amine structure at seed-0 evaluation 211 scores 3.2151129360788796e-21. A late four-ring, 35-heavy-atom amide expansion at seed-2 evaluation 296 scores only 0.00015241757289843227. The trifluoromethyl-containing ether/anilide at evaluation 299 scores 0.18573410909422844, so aromaticity, an amide and halogen substitution alone do not reproduce the leading arrangement. These are observed associations, not isolated substitution experiments.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer appearances have medians of 33 heavy atoms, 450.43 Da and four aromatic rings. Every one of the twelve digest leaders is a seed-2 substituted arylamino/phenyl quinazoline with butoxy and methoxy groups: 34 to 41 heavy atoms, four aromatic rings and one shared exact Murcko scaffold. The full trajectories are broader, with 355 distinct nonempty Murcko scaffolds. Seed 0 ends with a substituted pyridyl/dinitrophenyl hydrazone as its recorded leader, whereas seed 1 favors an imino, anilino and cyano-substituted fused aza-ring system. Thus the seed-2 family should not be mistaken for the whole panel. The leading quinazolines are plausible aromatic medicinal scaffolds, but their aromatic area, alkoxy appendages and halogen content give substantial hydrophobic bulk. All three trajectories are identical to the Parent.
liabilities: Four aromatic rings, multiple alkoxy groups and extensive halogenation can produce bulky hydrophobic structures; measured solubility and useful exposure are not supplied.

The secondary ether appendage in the 590.04-Da cited leader at seed-2 evaluation 268 has an unassigned tetrahedral centre. The full task contains 99 optimizer appearances with unassigned perceived centres and no explicit stereochemical tags.

The low-tail long-chain quaternary ammonium is structurally closer to a surfactant than to the leading heteroaromatic family. Other seeds also expose hydrazone/imine-form questions, so the highest-score family does not describe every proposed chemical form.
missing_features: Alternative cores retaining the successful arylamino/aza-aromatic/ether attachment relationships are absent from the twelve leading examples, despite broader exploration elsewhere in the trajectories.

Successful exploration of nonplanar ring architectures is not shown by this leading family. Its reward pattern supplies no basis for prescribing one unseen reference scaffold or assuming that more halogens would close the remaining gap.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Recorded final-best scores are 0.5998615059406662, 0.6263699396108253 and 0.6669492630755185 for seeds 0, 1 and 2. Within the cited seed-2 family, the trifluorophenyl leader scores 0.6669492630755185 and the difluorophenyl analogue 0.6666996765035981. Increasing to the cited tetrafluorophenyl form yields 0.6534013806124255, and a different difluoro placement yields 0.6362655153804642. The butyl-linked final analogue scores 0.6316114681166585, below the butoxy-linked leader. Reward therefore tracks the arrangement of the arylamino, aza-aromatic and ether-linked decorations more closely than a simple preference for more fluorine or carbon. Plausible sulfone-containing quinoline and indole structures score 0.28535067873303166 and 0.28799019607843135. The long-chain quaternary ammonium scores 0.5 and hexanol 0.5008612522607871; that relatively high floor cannot be interpreted as comparable medicinal chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer appearances have medians of 28 heavy atoms, 389.20 Da, three rings and two aromatic rings. The twelve leaders contain 25 to 30 heavy atoms and three to five rings; eight contain a piperazine. Seed 0 supplies lipophilic biaryl/benzyl piperazines, including the brominated propyl-substituted leader. Seed 1 supplies phenolic or methoxybenzyl secondary amines connected by alkyl chains to difluorobenzazepine or arylpiperazine units. Seed 2 supplies aromatic ketones or amides bearing a phenoxypropylpiperidine arm and a second aromatic appendage. These are recognizable medicinal-chemistry architectures containing potentially basic saturated nitrogens, rather than a shortage of cyclic amines. Compared with Parent n-c2ef5c1d5a78, the four oxygen-adjacent chloromethyl forms are absent, while methoxy, phenoxy and aryl-halide chemistry remains. Only the seed-1 trajectory differs, beginning at evaluation 249; all recorded endpoint best scores remain identical.
liabilities: Lipophilic biaryl/halogen substituents and several potentially ionizable nitrogens create unresolved solubility and solution-microstate questions; neutral SMILES do not demonstrate a single neutral species.
Long alkyl and ether-rich chains add conformational freedom, illustrated by the lower-scoring final long-linker amide.

The twelve cited leaders have no RDKit-perceived unassigned tetrahedral centres, so their lack of @ tags is not itself a stereochemical defect. The broader task contains 190 appearances with unassigned centres. Absence of the Parent chloromethyl forms is a narrower observation than general chemical stability.
missing_features: The low-scoring structures often lack the exposed saturated amine/aromatic attachment relationship already present in the leaders. The generator can produce that relationship but does not consistently retain it while changing ring systems or linkers.

The high-scoring set already contains basic cyclic amines and multiple aromatic contacts; these observations do not justify prescribing another amine, a particular unseen receptor interaction or one uniquely missing pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The brominated biaryl/benzyl piperazine scores 0.9999997933663268 and the phenol-linked difluorobenzazepine diamine scores 0.9999997851052089. Lower examples retain aromatic rings but put nitrogen in amide or sulfonamide environments: the amide/sulfonyl-piperidine structure scores 1.9828327575562915e-05 and the acylated piperidine carboxamide scores 2.6715842904959654e-05. The observed separation is consistent with accessible basic amine placement combined with aromatic bulk, not nitrogen count alone. In the final seed-2 examples, the smaller amino ketone lacking the phenoxypropylpiperidine arm scores 0.0035116287191461495, while the arm-bearing amino ketone scores 0.999988872643426. A longer ether-rich amide with 17 RDKit rotatable bonds scores 0.5728095677025575, whereas the shorter ketone with nine scores 0.9999937368364026. Thus adding flexible polar linker material does not uniformly help. Scores near their observed ceiling cannot resolve a missing binding interaction or establish experimental binding.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer appearances have medians of 24 heavy atoms, 340.03 Da and three rings, with broad exact-core coverage: 732 nonempty Murcko scaffolds. The leaders nevertheless show a recurring chemical arrangement: ten of the twelve have a sulfonamide and eleven contain a piperazine. The best is a 32-heavy-atom, 475.55-Da bis-sulfonyl piperazine connecting a methylquinoline and a benzodioxole, with five perceived rings in total. Both piperazine nitrogens are sulfonylated, so this leading example must not be described as a freely basic piperazine. Other leaders use an N-methyl piperazine, an aryl sulfonamide, or benzodioxole-linked alkyl chains. Most of these scaffolds have plausible conventional synthetic connections, while a partially unsaturated N-rich ring and much larger repeated sulfonyl assemblies make the whole output more mixed. All 900 molecule/score records match the Parent.
liabilities: The 628.80-Da two-piperazine leader illustrates repeated sulfonyl and ring accumulation, which increases molecular and polar-group burden without surpassing the more compact leading arrangement.

The ringless azide and N-hydroxy trichloromethyl form are chemically distinct from ordinary stable medicinal scaffolds and merit attachment-specific scrutiny; their low reward alone is not a synthesis assay.

A sulfonyl fluoride persists at seed-0 evaluation 289 with observed score 0.15884700241362154. This is a recognizable reactive functional handle, not proof of invalid chemistry or a reason to ban all heteroatom-halogen bonds. It is outside the removed oxygen-adjacent carbon-halide form.
missing_features: Many proposals lack the connected sulfonyl/cyclic-diamine/aromatic arrangement seen in the leaders; isolated small polar fragments or a lone piperazine-bearing ring do not reproduce it.

Useful recombination of that arrangement remains inconsistent despite extensive scaffold exploration. The trajectories do not identify an unseen reference pair or prove that increasing basicity, adding another sulfonyl group or maximizing raw scaffold count would improve the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methylquinoline/bis-sulfonyl-piperazine/benzodioxole leader scores 0.2588686674995393. The smaller methylquinoline sulfonyl-N-methylpiperazine scores 0.2272296156064184, whereas the more elaborate two-piperazine, 41-heavy-atom assembly scores 0.2301209791058402. A compact sulfonamide-linked benzodioxole/piperazine example scores 0.2229480268629566. These examples favor a combined cyclic-diamine, sulfonyl and aromatic arrangement, but do not support indefinite multiplication of those groups or a requirement for a free basic nitrogen. The six low-tail digest examples are all ringless: allyl azide scores 0.0, the sulfur-linked diacid 0.02095188685475281, and the small sulfur-oxo acid 0.02668612498071339. A final small pyrrole/piperazine structure scores 0.10826206026353223. Ring presence and piperazine alone therefore do not recover the fuller leading arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer appearances have medians of 24 heavy atoms, 347.09 Da and three rings, but the twelve leaders range from one to four rings and 20 to 26 heavy atoms. The seed-2 leader is a secondary-amino acylsulfonamide attached to a fluoro/trifluoromethyl phenyl group. Other strong examples include a branched amino-amide/oxalamide, arylsulfonyl cyclic amidines bearing ester or imidate substituents, a guanidine-bearing benzofused amine, a sulfonyl pyrrolidinone and a quinolone acylthiourea. The leaders occupy eight exact nonempty Murcko scaffolds; the full proposals occupy 774. This is broad but chemically uneven exploration, including large peptide-like chains and densely decorated aromatic or polycyclic outliers. Ordinary amide and sulfonamide chemistry is plentiful, while some leading imidate, hydrazone, thiourea and amidine forms have additional state and attachment questions. Parent comparison changes only five seed-1 molecule/score records; the oxygen-adjacent bromo-ring form is absent and all three endpoint-best scores remain the same.
liabilities: Large peptide-like chains and polycyclic expansions combine size, conformational complexity and frequently undefined stereochemistry. The complete task has 273 optimizer appearances with unassigned centres.

The acylsulfonamide, imidate, sulfonyl hydrazone, guanidine and acylthiourea examples have different acid/base, tautomer and attachment chemistry. Their SMILES and rewards do not establish a shared solution state or validated stability.

The fluorinated branched amino-amide is a credible compact chemotype, but its potentially stereogenic centre is unspecified. Merely omitting the oxygen-adjacent bromo attachment seen in the Parent does not resolve this broader representation gap.
missing_features: Consistent delivery of moderate-sized molecules with the useful amino/amide/sulfonyl attachment relationships is missing across much of the trajectory; both large repeated polar chains and small poorly arranged polar structures score weakly.

Four of the twelve leaders have RDKit-perceived unassigned tetrahedral centres, including the branched amino-amide and guanidine-bearing fused ring. No stereochemical configurations are explored explicitly, although these trajectories do not establish a score benefit for doing so.
The available high-scoring examples span several distinct chemotypes. No unique absent target heterocycle, substitution pattern or pharmacophore can be inferred from these scores alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact amino-acylsulfonamide scores 0.32609684308650033 and the branched amino-amide/oxalamide 0.3085499097640706. The fluoroaryl cyclic-amidine ester scores 0.3034617343186778, its cited imidate counterpart 0.2795168707513844, and the corresponding nonfluorinated aryl ester 0.24905607529893223. A nonfluorinated guanidine-bearing fused ring still scores 0.2711448282680827, and the quinolone acylthiourea scores 0.26424211308214746. The common signal is an appropriate combination of moderate size and polar-group arrangement across several scaffolds, not an obligatory fluorinated core. The six low-tail examples have 40 to 61 heavy atoms and molecular weights from 572.56 to 863.92 Da, including peptide-like and long-chain structures with zero or extremely small reward. Size reduction alone also fails: the final 18-heavy-atom carbonyl-rich heterocycle at evaluation 297 scores 2.6445959326166367e-17. The digest median is reported as 0.0; the examples do not identify which hidden objective component limits reward.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All 4,350 optimizer strings lack @ and directional alkene markers. Passive perception finds 843 appearances containing 1,428 unassigned tetrahedral centres. Cited high-scoring examples include a branched amino-amide at 0.3085499097640706, a guanidine-bearing fused ring at 0.2711448282680827, a sulfinamide at 0.4531317717091581 and a secondary ether appendage at 0.6546458319881191. Some leading families are achiral, so the gap applies to eligible structures rather than every molecule.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces potentially stereogenic structures without expressing their configurations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent eligible configurations during de novo generation while retaining coherent connectivity and canonical identity. Distinguish genuinely stereogenic centres and configurationally meaningful bonds from achiral structures, and let observed feedback establish where configuration matters; no universal stereochemical score gain follows from the present data.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The full proposal panel contains 2,806 distinct nonempty exact Murcko scaffolds, yet twelve leading decorated aza-aromatic examples share one scaffold and differ mainly in aryl halogen and alkoxy decorations. Other leading groups repeatedly reuse aromatic amides or sulfonyl-linked cyclic diamines. Thus missing ring chemistry is not the issue; useful relationships between rings, linkers and polar centres become concentrated in a few families.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad scaffold exploration does not reliably extend the attachment arrangements of successful families into alternative cores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support changes to ring architecture and linker topology while preserving the useful chemical attachment relationships found in accepted observations. Assess whether the resulting evaluated families retain those relationships and useful reward; increasing an exact scaffold count by itself is insufficient, and no fixed reference core or objective identity is required.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A compact three-aromatic-ring amide scores 0.5 while a later 35-heavy-atom repeated-amide expansion scores 0.00015241757289843227. A long ether-rich amide with 17 rotatable bonds scores 0.5728095677025575 while a shorter arm-bearing ketone with nine scores 0.9999937368364026. A 41-heavy-atom repeated sulfonyl/piperazine assembly scores 0.2301209791058402 versus 0.2588686674995393 for a smaller connected arrangement. Conversely, small ringless fragments and a small carbonyl-rich heterocycle also score poorly, so these observations do not support a universal small-molecule preference.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent control of appendage growth, linker length and polar-group repetition within otherwise promising structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make appendage size, linker spacing and polar-group density adjustable without losing productive ring/amine/amide or sulfonyl connections. Use the generator's own task-local feedback to learn appropriate combinations rather than applying an unconditional size cap, removing all polar groups or repeating a favorable fragment indefinitely.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The specified oxygen-adjacent saturated carbon bearing Cl, Br or I is absent from 4,350 Child optimizer appearances versus five in the Parent, but the digest still contains an alpha-bromoacrylamide, an azide, an N-hydroxy trichloromethyl form, sulfonyl hydrazones, an imidate and an acylthiourea. A trajectory also retains one sulfonyl fluoride. Several unusual heteroatom-containing leaders have substantial reward, and ordinary amides, sulfonamides, ethers and aryl halides are widespread. These are distinguishable chemical contexts, not a single class of invalid or unstable molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: Excluding one narrowly defined attachment form leaves heterogeneous reactive handles and unresolved chemical states in the generated output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Develop attachment-aware representation of complete chemical forms, including plausible valence, local functional-group context and explicit state or configuration where relevant. Preserve conventional heteroatom and halogen chemistry, and distinguish intentional reactive handles from accidental attachment combinations. Any further form constraint needs evaluated evidence; the current narrow absence does not establish improved synthesis, stability or reward.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

method_references.title: Thomas, M., O'Boyle, N. M., Bender, A., and de Graaf, C. (2022). Augmented Hill-Climb increases reinforcement learning efficiency for language-based de novo molecule generation. Journal of Cheminformatics 14, 68.
